title: Waypoint Gridside: tiled navigation & contextual gateway prototype
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: Current console sidebar and workspace switching patterns are increasingly brittle for multi-tenant customers and power users. Long lists, ambiguous routing for nested dashboards, and modal workspace switches cause cognitive load and slow task flows (create model -> view rollout -> inspect cost lens).

Proposal summary: Introduce a tiled, grid-style side surface ("Waypoint Gridside") that surfaces contextual gateways: compact route cards that combine destination, recent state, and a micro-action (open, pin, probe). The gridside sits in the left-rail footprint but can expand to a transient canvas for keyboard-first navigation. It de-emphasizes deep tree drilling in favor of direct, predictable entry points into dashboards, rollouts, and cost views.

Design goals:
- Reduce time-to-destination for 80% common tasks (open dashboard, inspect model rollouts, view cost breakdown) by 25% in lab tasks.
- Surface recently active routes and actionable affordances (pin, compare, open in split) without full route duplication.
- Preserve discoverability for nested routes (project > model > rollout > eval) via progressive disclosure and in-card breadcrumbs.
- Keyboard-first support and accessible focus order for power users.
- Lightweight telemetry hooks for gradual rollout and A/B testing (open rate, route completion, quick-switch latency).

Scope included in this ticket:
- High-fidelity Figma prototype for Gridside collapsed/expanded states (desktop).
- Interaction spec for keyboard navigation, focus management, and micro-actions.
- Content patterns for route cards (title, subline, status chip, micro-actions).
- Mid-fidelity flows for workspace quick-switch that preserves in-progress drafts and local console state.
- Prototype usability script and success metrics.

Out of scope (this ticket):
- Mobile nav rework (separate workstream).
- Backend routing rewrite; engineering will adapt surface-level route mapping and telemetry.

Why this differs from previous work: Waypoint Gridside replaces long vertical lists with spatial tiles that encode state and affordances. Unlike prior "sidebar compression" approaches, this prototype focuses on temporal signals (recently used) and on-the-card micro-actions to reduce context switching.

Design artifacts: Figma prototype, interaction spec, low-fidelity motion frames, usability script, rollout measurement plan. Links in attachments.

Acceptance criteria:
- Figma prototype demonstrates: collapsed Gridside, expanded grid canvas, route card variants for dashboard/rollout/cost, keyboard focus sequence, and split-open flows.
- PM signoff on task time reduction targets and A/B plan.
- Engineering acknowledges constraints for ephemeral canvas and agrees on telemetry events.
- Usability study (n=8 internal sessions) completed and documented with at least 6/8 participants completing core tasks under target time improvements.
comments: 2026-02-21 - Maya Patel: Initial kickoff. Aligned with PM and Eng leadership on scope. Decided to prototype on desktop first and validate keyboard flow. Asked Eng to sketch rough constraints around route mapping and persisted state.
2026-02-26 - Jordan Kim: Uploaded first Figma frames (collapsed + expanded). Added three card types: dashboard, rollout, cost-view. Requesting feedback on chip semantics and pin behavior.

2026-03-01 - Liam O'Connor (PM): Reviewed. Likes surface of recent rollouts. Concern: need clear affordance for pinned vs. workspace-synced items. Suggested adding small lock icon to indicate workspace-scoped pins. Added acceptance criteria about preserving drafts when switching workspaces.

2026-03-03 - Noah Chen (Eng): Reviewed interaction notes. Notes on constraints: splitting the canvas open requires a route alias layer in the router; we can implement a transient route map using query params to avoid full backend changes. Agreed to emit telemetry events: gridside.open, card.open, card.pin, quickswitch.complete.

2026-03-05 - Sofia Reyes (UX Research): Ran three guerrilla sessions with internal PMs. Observations: participants used micro-actions heavily when shown, felt less confident when cards lacked in-card breadcrumbs. Recommended in-card 2-level breadcrumb and hover reveal of nested children.

2026-03-07 - Jordan Kim: Prototype updated with in-card breadcrumbs + hover child list. Adjusted keyboard sequence to include quick-action keybindings (G then number to open nth card). Added motion frames for expand/collapse.

2026-03-09 - Design review: Team requested accessibility pass for ARIA roles and focus management. Decided to add a11y checklist and include a developer hand-off session. PM approved A/B experiment for 10% of org to start after engineering integration.
2026-03-10 - Maya Patel: Marking ticket for formal review. Next: schedule dev hand-off, finalize telemetry schema, and draft rollout communication sample for customers.
acceptance_criteria: Figma shows collapsed Gridside + expanded canvas + route card variants
Keyboard-first sequence documented and validated in prototype
Telemetry events agreed and documented with Eng
Usability test (n>=8) demonstrates target time reduction or yields clear next steps
PM sign-off and engineering acknowledgement for phased rollout
